newsitem.title: POLAND: TENDER FOR POLISH HANDLOWY SALE ADVISER BY YR-END.
newsitem.headline: TENDER FOR POLISH HANDLOWY SALE ADVISER BY YR-END.

text.p: The Polish Finance Ministry wants to announce a tender for an adviser in the planned sale of the country's biggest commercial Bank Handlowy SA by the end of this year, a senior ministry official said.
"Early in December we should decide how to choose the adviser and the tender should be announced still this year," Wieslaw Federowicz, the head of the ministry's banking department, told Reuters.
"We want to find such a tender procedure, which would allow to pick the adviser as quickly as possible," he added.

Federowicz also said that the bank's privatisation, in which more than 50 percent of Handlowy's shares would be transferred to private investors, including a 15-percent employee tranche, should be completed by the end of 1997.
Federowicz said the ministry's tentative plan aimed to begin with an offer of Bank Handlowy shares to foreign investors, which later would be followed by a public offer.
"For the time being we assume that we would start with an offer for foreign investors and later on with a public offering," he said.
But he added it would be up to the government to decide on the way Bank Handlowy, the country's leading commercial bank, would be privatised and that the decision was likely early next month.
Handlowy netted 390.3 million zlotys in the first half of this year and had a balance sheet total of 10.46 billion zlotys.
